items.title: 8.8 Equilibrium constant and position of equilibrium

source_refs.note: Topic 8.8, printed pages 173-174, with Quick Check 8.4 (a) as the self-check. The print's '[A]^n [B]^b' is read as [A]^a [B]^b.

blocks.title: Position of equilibrium
blocks.text: The position of equilibrium refers to the relative amounts of products and reactants present in an equilibrium mixture.

In 1864 the Norwegian chemists C. Guldberg (1836-1902) and P. Waage (1833-1900) measured the compositions of many reaction systems at equilibrium and found that for any reversible reaction the ratio of the product of the equilibrium concentrations of the products, each raised to its coefficient in the balanced equation, to the product of the equilibrium concentrations of the reactants, each raised to its coefficient, is always a constant under a given set of conditions. For the general reaction aA + bB giving cC + dD, Kc = [C]^c [D]^d / [A]^a [B]^b. By the law of mass action the rate of a reaction is directly proportional to the active masses of the reactants, raised to the coefficients of the balanced equation; active mass means the molar concentration in mol dm-3, written in square brackets.

For A + B giving C + D, the forward rate = kf [A][B], where kf is the forward rate constant, and the reverse rate = kr [C][D], where kr is the reverse rate constant. At equilibrium the two rates are equal, kf [A][B] = kr [C][D], so kf / kr = [C][D] / [A][B]. The left side is a ratio of two constants, so it is another constant, the equilibrium constant Kc: Kc = [C][D] / [A][B], the equilibrium constant expression. For aA + bB giving cC + dD, with coefficients a, b, c and d, Kc = [C]^c [D]^d / [A]^a [B]^b.

blocks.caption: The equilibrium constant, its four forms, their relations and units, with the chapter's sample calculations (original diagram after topics 8.8 to 8.9).
blocks.long_description: Setting the forward rate kf [A][B] equal to the reverse rate kr [C][D] gives kf / kr = [C][D] / [A][B], a constant called Kc, and for general coefficients each concentration is raised to its coefficient. The same ratio can be written with partial pressures, moles or mole fractions, and the forms are linked through delta n, the change in gas moles; when delta n is zero all four are equal. Kc has no units when the mole numbers balance, as in ester formation (4.03), and carries units otherwise, as for ammonia (mol-2 dm6). Kp for ammonia at 773 K is far smaller than Kc because delta n is -2.
